prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a storefront display separated from the camera wearer by a glass partition (roughly 0.5–1.5 m away), behind which a long display table holding belts, hats, and boots sits at about 1.5–2.5 m, flanked on the right by a standing mannequin (~1.5–2 m away, ~0.3 m right of the table) and backed by clothing racks (~2.5–3.5 m away) and two distant headless mannequins on the far left (~4–5 m away). In frames 1–3, a very bright rounded region in the lower-left foreground (~0.2–0.4 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) captures a carried brown object or body part partially out of view at the bottom-left frame edge, while all store items and the front-facing mannequin (whose head is cropped out of frames 1–3 before coming into view facing forward and slightly left in frames 4–5) remain out of reach behind the glass. Across the five frames, the camera wearer shifts slightly right and angles upward and rightward toward the wooden glass door on the far right, causing the lower-left foreground object to exit the frame after frame 3 as the door frame (~1.5–2 m away) enters on the right. The depth map makes the planar surface of the glass storefront and the immediate proximity of the lower-left foreground object much clearer than the RGB image alone, where the transparent glass and red 'SALE' lettering visually merge with the interior objects. However, the map is unreliable across frames 3–5, where reflections and transparency on the glass pane cause the estimator to wash out the interior table, clothing racks, and mannequin into an indistinct, overly bright planar fog.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies the spatial layout of the foreground display and figures, labeling the lower-left foreground object at ~0.2–0.4 m (within the camera wearer's arm's reach and partly cropped by the bottom-left border) as a 'person' in frames 1–3, the central display table at ~1.5–2.5 m as a 'dining table' in frames 1–2, and the standing mannequin just right of the table (~1.5–2 m away, facing toward the camera wearer and slightly left with its head occluded by the top frame edge in frames 1–3) as a 'person' in frames 1–3 and 5. In frames 1–2, it also segments the two background mannequins standing ~4–5 m away behind and to the left of the clothing racks (~2.5 m behind the table and ~1 m apart from each other, facing toward the storefront) as 'person' instances before they exit the left side of the view as the camera pans right. As the camera turns rightward and tilts slightly in frames 3–5, the table mask disappears, the lower-left foreground mask leaves the frame after frame 3, and the right-hand mannequin shifts slightly leftward in the frame while remaining ~1.5–2 m away next to the right-side doorway. Compared to the RGB strip, the segmentation map clearly isolates the silhouettes of the distant upper-left mannequins and separates the foreground table surface from the dense clothing racks behind it. However, the map is highly unreliable under motion blur and glass reflections in frames 3–5, missing all masks in frame 4 and misclassifying the right-hand tan boot on the table as a 'bottle' in frame 3 and a 'banana' in frame 5, the blue beret on the table as a 'sink', and vertical clothing strips on the rack as a 'surfboard' and 'umbrella'.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames because the human-shaped figures in the scene are store mannequins rather than live people, and the camera wearer's own body and hands remain mostly out of view below the camera. In frame 1, a compact cluster of yellow body keypoints appears in the lower-left foreground on the edge of the display table (~1.8 m away, below the red 'A' decal and left of the belts), and in frame 5, a distorted yellow partial skeleton appears near the bottom-center over the tan boots and sweater stack on the right side of the table (~1.8 m away, ~0.5 m left of the standing mannequin). Across the five frames, as the camera wearer pans rightward from the left display window toward the right entrance door, no poses are tracked on the standing mannequin on the right (~1.5–2 m away, facing forward toward the glass) or on the two distant mannequins on the far left (~4–5 m away), and no magenta hand skeletons appear anywhere within arm's reach of the camera wearer or the figures. This absence of valid skeletons helps confirm that the standing figures in the RGB scene are static mannequins rather than people looking at or interacting with the camera wearer. At the same time, the map is unreliable where it hallucinates spurious yellow body keypoints onto inanimate merchandise on the table in frames 1 and 5 while failing to register the human-shaped mannequins.
